goldenPoints: Congo red with apple-green birefringence diagnoses amyloidosis — AL in myeloma, beta-2 microglobulin in dialysis patients
Mentzer index below 13 means thalassaemia trait; above 13 means iron deficiency
Sickle cell anaemia is a single point mutation: glutamate replaced by valine at position 6 of the beta chain
Philadelphia chromosome t(9;22) BCR-ABL defines CML and is its investigation of choice
Calcitonin is the tumour marker of medullary thyroid carcinoma; RET mutation causes it
Type 2 lepra reaction (ENL) and SLE are type III hypersensitivity; transfusion reactions are type II
Bernard-Soulier = GPIb defect with giant platelets; Glanzmann = GPIIb/IIIa defect
B12 deficiency raises methylmalonic acid and damages the cord; folate deficiency does neither
Myeloma = CRAB: hypercalcaemia, renal failure, anaemia, lytic bone lesions with an M spike
Orphan Annie eye nuclei + psammoma bodies = papillary thyroid carcinoma
intro: Pathology carries 13 questions in every 300-question FMGE paper, and the previous-year papers show one clear pattern: blood dominates. Anaemias, leukaemias and bleeding disorders fill nearly half the stems, with amyloidosis, hypersensitivity types, genetic disorders and tumour markers close behind. Use these notes topic by topic, then test yourself with the flashcards.
subject: Pathology
tagline: FMGE asks haematology first, then amyloid, hypersensitivity, tumour markers and translocations

topics.askedAs: irreversible injury features, necrosis types, healing sequence
topics.oneLiner: Brain liquefies, heart coagulates, TB caseates — and neutrophils always reach the wound first.
points: Irreversible injury: membrane damage, lysosomal rupture, amorphous densities in mitochondria, karyolysis/pyknosis/karyorrhexis
Reversible injury: cell swelling, fatty change, membrane blebs, clumped chromatin — ATP depletion is the central event
Liquefactive necrosis: brain infarcts and abscesses; coagulative necrosis: solid-organ infarcts (heart, kidney, spleen)
Caseous necrosis = TB; fat necrosis = acute pancreatitis (saponification); fibrinoid necrosis = vessel walls in vasculitis
Apoptotic bodies contain fragmented nucleus and cytoplasmic blebs — no inflammation, single cells, caspase-driven
Neutrophils are the first cells to arrive in acute inflammation; macrophages dominate by 48 hours
Leukocyte adhesion: selectins roll, integrins grip, PECAM-1 (CD31) guides transmigration
Wound healing order: haemostasis → inflammation → proliferation (granulation tissue) → remodelling/maturation
Granulation tissue = proliferating fibroblasts + new thin-walled capillaries in loose matrix
topics.title: Cell Injury, Inflammation & Wound Healing
topics.trap: Apoptosis has NO inflammation; necrosis always does. Examiners swap this constantly.

topics.askedAs: amyloid type matched to the clinical setting
topics.oneLiner: Congo red, apple-green: AL = light chain/myeloma, AA = chronic inflammation, beta-2M = dialysis.
points: Universal stain: Congo red → apple-green birefringence under polarised light
AL amyloid = immunoglobulin light chains; seen in multiple myeloma and plasma cell dyscrasias
AA amyloid = serum amyloid A; secondary to chronic inflammation (TB, rheumatoid arthritis, bronchiectasis)
Beta-2 microglobulin amyloid = long-term haemodialysis; carpal tunnel and joints
Dialysis dementia itself is aluminium toxicity — but the amyloid of dialysis patients is beta-2 microglobulin type
ATTR = transthyretin; wild type causes senile cardiac amyloidosis in elderly men
Cardiac amyloidosis gives restrictive cardiomyopathy with low-voltage ECG despite thick walls
Amyloid is extracellular, beta-pleated sheet protein, resistant to proteolysis
topics.title: Amyloidosis
topics.trap: Haemodialysis amyloid is beta-2 microglobulin, NOT AL — the most repeated swap in this topic.

topics.askedAs: Virchow triad, embolus types, shock features
topics.oneLiner: Virchow's triad builds the clot; falling urine output is the first whisper of shock.
points: Virchow triad: endothelial injury, stasis/turbulent flow, hypercoagulability
Lines of Zahn (alternating pale platelet-fibrin and red cell layers) prove a thrombus formed in flowing blood
Most common embolus = thromboembolus from deep leg veins; most common site of impaction = pulmonary arteries
Fat embolism: after long-bone fracture — dyspnoea, petechiae, confusion at 24-72 hours
Early (compensated) hypovolaemic shock: urine output falls first as kidneys are sacrificed to protect brain and heart
All shock types share inadequate tissue perfusion and cellular hypoxia at the end stage
Oedema in nephrotic syndrome = low oncotic pressure; in heart failure = raised hydrostatic pressure
Chronic passive congestion of liver gives the nutmeg liver appearance
topics.title: Haemodynamics, Thrombosis & Shock
topics.trap: Amniotic fluid embolism causes DIC; air embolism is the caisson/diver one — do not interchange them.

topics.askedAs: lab pattern BT/PT/aPTT matched to the disease
topics.oneLiner: Normal platelets + long aPTT = haemophilia; normal count + long bleeding time = vWD or a platelet-function defect.
points: Calcium (factor IV) is essential for converting prothrombin to thrombin — chelate it and blood cannot clot
Tissue factor (factor III) initiates the extrinsic cascade after trauma
von Willebrand factor carries factor VIII and bridges platelets to collagen via GPIb
Bernard-Soulier syndrome: defect in platelet GPIb — giant platelets, prolonged bleeding time
Glanzmann thrombasthenia: defect in GPIIb/IIIa — platelets cannot aggregate
Haemophilia A = factor VIII deficiency (X-linked); aPTT prolonged, bleeding time and platelets normal
HSP (IgA vasculitis): non-blanching rash on legs/buttocks, arthritis, abdominal pain, haematuria — platelet count NORMAL
ITP: isolated low platelets, anti-platelet antibodies, splenectomy helps refractory cases
DIC: everything consumed — platelets and fibrinogen low, PT/aPTT prolonged, D-dimer high, schistocytes seen
topics.title: Platelet & Coagulation Disorders
topics.trap: A vasculitis rash (HSP) does NOT blanch and platelets are normal — thrombocytopenic purpura always has low platelets.

topics.askedAs: Mentzer index, koilonychia, B12 vs folate neurology
topics.oneLiner: Mentzer below 13 = thalassaemia; B12 hurts nerves and raises MMA, folate does neither.
points: Iron deficiency is the most common cause of microcytic anaemia — koilonychia, cheilosis, Plummer-Vinson syndrome
Mentzer index (MCV ÷ RBC count) < 13 favours thalassaemia trait; > 13 favours iron deficiency
Thalassaemia major: hepatosplenomegaly, chipmunk facies, hair-on-end skull, target cells, raised HbF
Anaemia of chronic disease: hepcidin blocks ferroportin, trapping iron in macrophages — IL-6 drives hepcidin
Sideroblastic anaemia: ring sideroblasts in marrow, iron OVERLOAD despite anaemia (lead poisoning is a cause)
Basophilic stippling of RBCs = lead poisoning (also thalassaemia)
B12 deficiency: neurological signs (subacute combined degeneration), raised methylmalonic acid AND homocysteine
Folate deficiency: raised homocysteine only, methylmalonic acid normal, NO neurological signs
MCV very high (e.g. 160 fL) with normal methylmalonyl-CoA points to folate, not B12, deficiency
topics.title: Microcytic & Macrocytic Anaemias
topics.trap: Never give folate alone in B12 deficiency — the anaemia improves while the cord damage worsens.

topics.askedAs: smear finding or Coombs result matched to cause
topics.oneLiner: Spherocytes + positive Coombs = immune; spherocytes + negative Coombs + family history = hereditary spherocytosis.
points: Sickle cell anaemia: glutamic acid → valine at position 6 of beta chain (point mutation, Glu6Val)
Hydroxyurea raises fetal haemoglobin (HbF) and reduces sickle crises
Hereditary spherocytosis: spectrin/ankyrin defect, spherocytes, osmotic fragility increased — splenectomy is curative
G6PD deficiency: Heinz bodies, bite cells, haemolysis after fava beans, primaquine, infections; X-linked
Warm AIHA = IgG, Coombs (DAT) positive, spherocytes; cold AIHA = IgM, Mycoplasma/EBV linked
Haemolysis labs: raised unconjugated bilirubin, raised LDH, raised reticulocytes, LOW haptoglobin
PNH: PIGA gene defect, loss of CD55/CD59, complement-mediated haemolysis, morning haemoglobinuria
Penicillin-induced immune haemolysis is a type II hypersensitivity reaction
Microangiopathic haemolysis (HUS/TTP/DIC) shows schistocytes — fragmented RBCs
topics.title: Haemolytic Anaemias & Haemoglobinopathies
topics.trap: Haptoglobin falls in haemolysis; it RISES in inflammation (it is an acute-phase reactant) — context decides.

topics.askedAs: translocation, age group and one classic lab value
topics.oneLiner: t(9;22) CML, t(15;17) APL, t(8;14) Burkitt, t(2;5) ALCL — translocations are free marks.
points: CML: t(9;22) Philadelphia chromosome, BCR-ABL fusion — investigation of choice is cytogenetics/FISH for BCR-ABL; massive splenomegaly with TLC around 1,00,000+ and basophilia is the classic picture; imatinib treats it
Myelofibrosis: teardrop RBCs (dacrocytes), leukoerythroblastic picture, giant platelets, dry tap on aspiration
AML: Auer rods in blasts; APL t(15;17) PML-RARA with DIC — treated with ATRA
ALL: commonest childhood malignancy; TdT positive blasts; good prognosis subtype is hyperdiploid
CLL: elderly, smudge cells on smear, absolute lymphocytosis
Burkitt lymphoma: t(8;14) c-MYC, starry-sky appearance, jaw mass in the African child
Hodgkin lymphoma: Reed-Sternberg cells (owl-eye nuclei), CD15 and CD30 positive
Anaplastic large cell lymphoma: t(2;5) NPM-ALK, hallmark cells
Essential thrombocythaemia: isolated very high platelets, JAK2 mutation, marrow shows increased megakaryocytes
topics.title: Leukaemias & Lymphomas
topics.trap: Starry sky is Burkitt lymphoma (macrophages among tumour cells) — not Hodgkin lymphoma.

topics.askedAs: CRAB features, M protein, lytic lesions
topics.oneLiner: Old man + back pain + lytic lesions + M spike = myeloma; think CRAB.
points: Myeloma triad of clues: elderly patient, back pain, punched-out lytic bone lesions, marrow plasma cells > 10%
CRAB: hyperCalcaemia, Renal failure, Anaemia, Bone lesions
Bence Jones proteins = free light chains in urine; may be missed on routine dipstick
Serum electrophoresis shows a monoclonal M spike in the gamma region
Rouleaux formation on peripheral smear from excess paraprotein
Most common cause of death in myeloma = infection; renal failure is the second major killer
Amyloidosis (AL type) is the myeloma-linked deposition disease to pair with it
Hyperviscosity syndrome is the classic complication of Waldenström macroglobulinaemia (IgM), not myeloma
topics.title: Multiple Myeloma & Plasma Cell Disorders
topics.trap: Myeloma lesions are purely lytic with a COLD bone scan — osteoblastic lesions point to prostate cancer.

topics.askedAs: marker or gene matched to the tumour
topics.oneLiner: Calcitonin–medullary thyroid, AFP–HCC, RET–MEN 2, APC–FAP, mismatch repair–Lynch.
points: Calcitonin is the marker of medullary thyroid carcinoma (from parafollicular C cells)
AFP: hepatocellular carcinoma and yolk sac tumour; beta-hCG: choriocarcinoma
Acid phosphatase was the classic prostate cancer enzyme (now PSA); PSA is organ-specific, not cancer-specific
RET proto-oncogene mutation = medullary thyroid carcinoma and MEN 2
HNPCC/Lynch syndrome = mismatch repair gene defect (microsatellite instability) — colon plus endometrial cancers
Tumour suppressor genes (APC, RB) follow Knudson's two-hit rule; APC loss (chromosome 5) causes familial adenomatous polyposis — colon cancer inevitable without colectomy
Marfan syndrome: fibrillin-1 (FBN1) defect — tall habitus, arachnodactyly, upward lens dislocation, aortic root dilatation
Barrett oesophagus: squamous epithelium replaced by intestinal-type columnar epithelium (metaplasia) — premalignant
Psammoma bodies: papillary thyroid carcinoma, meningioma, serous ovarian tumours, mesothelioma
topics.title: Neoplasia: Genes, Syndromes & Tumour Markers
topics.trap: Psammoma bodies + Orphan Annie nuclei = papillary thyroid cancer; psammoma bodies in a dural tumour = meningioma.

topics.askedAs: MEN components, thyroid histology, pheo screening
topics.oneLiner: MEN 1 = 3 Ps (parathyroid, pituitary, pancreas); pheo is screened in urine as metanephrines/VMA.
points: MEN 1 (Wermer): parathyroid hyperplasia, pituitary adenoma, pancreatic islet tumours — commonest pancreatic tumour is gastrinoma overall, insulinoma is the commonest islet cell tumour type tested with MEN-1 stems
MEN 2A: medullary thyroid carcinoma + pheochromocytoma + parathyroid hyperplasia (RET gene)
Pheochromocytoma screening: urinary metanephrines and VMA (vanillylmandelic acid)
Papillary thyroid carcinoma: Orphan Annie eye nuclei, psammoma bodies, spreads via lymphatics
Hashimoto thyroiditis: Hürthle cells (abundant pink eosinophilic cytoplasm), anti-TPO antibodies, hypothyroidism
Conn syndrome (primary hyperaldosteronism): hypertension + hypokalaemia; muscle weakness — NOT hyperpigmentation
Kwashiorkor's specific feature: oedema with flaky-paint dermatosis and flag-sign hair — marasmus has no oedema
Wilson disease: ATP7B gene, low ceruloplasmin, Kayser-Fleischer rings, basal ganglia degeneration
Kartagener syndrome: dynein arm defect — situs inversus, sinusitis, bronchiectasis, infertility
topics.title: Endocrine & Metabolic Pathology
topics.trap: Hyperpigmentation belongs to Addison disease (ACTH), never to Conn syndrome — a favourite 'except' answer.

topics.askedAs: reaction type matched to the clinical vignette
topics.oneLiner: Bee sting = I, transfusion = II, SLE/ENL = III, contact dermatitis = IV.
points: Type I (IgE): anaphylaxis after bee sting or prawns — histamine is the chief early mediator; IgE is the culprit antibody
Type II (cytotoxic antibody): transfusion reactions, haemolytic disease of newborn (Coombs positive), penicillin haemolysis
Type III (immune complex): serum sickness, SLE, type 2 lepra reaction (ENL), Arthus reaction
Type IV (T-cell): contact dermatitis, tuberculin test, granulomas — the only antibody-free type
IgG is the most abundant immunoglobulin in serum; IgA dominates secretions; IgM is the largest and first formed
Sjögren syndrome: anti-Ro (SSA) and anti-La (SSB), dry eyes/mouth, Schirmer test < 5 mm in 5 minutes
Rheumatoid arthritis: anti-CCP is the most specific antibody; HLA-DR4 association
Reiter (reactive arthritis): HLA-B27 — also ankylosing spondylitis, psoriasis, IBD arthropathy
Chronic granulomatous disease: NADPH oxidase defect — recurrent catalase-positive infections and abscesses; SCID is combined B + T cell failure with infections of every type from infancy
topics.title: Immunopathology & Hypersensitivity
topics.trap: Type 2 lepra reaction (ENL) is type III hypersensitivity, not type IV — named in PYQs repeatedly.

topics.askedAs: antibody or biopsy finding matched to disease
topics.oneLiner: c-ANCA = Wegener, anti-dsDNA = SLE activity, Aschoff body = rheumatic fever.
points: SLE: anti-dsDNA (specific, tracks activity), anti-Smith (most specific), Libman-Sacks vegetations on BOTH valve surfaces
Coeliac disease: villous atrophy, anti-tissue transglutaminase IgA and anti-endomysial antibodies, linked to dermatitis herpetiformis
Granulomatosis with polyangiitis (Wegener): c-ANCA (anti-PR3) — sinusitis, haemoptysis, haematuria triad
Microscopic polyangiitis and eosinophilic GPA involve p-ANCA (anti-MPO)
Aschoff bodies are the pathognomonic lesion of rheumatic heart disease (Anitschkov 'caterpillar' cells)
Alzheimer disease: amyloid-beta plaques plus hyperphosphorylated tau tangles; tau also aggregates in frontotemporal dementia, while Parkinson disease deposits alpha-synuclein (Lewy bodies)
Hepatocellular carcinoma arises on HBV/HCV cirrhosis and aflatoxin exposure (p53 mutation); ground-glass hepatocytes mean HBsAg accumulation in hepatitis B
Light criteria separate exudative from transudative pleural effusion (protein and LDH ratios)
topics.title: Autoimmune Diseases & Systemic Pathology
topics.trap: Libman-Sacks vegetations sit on both sides of the valve; infective endocarditis vegetations favour the upstream surface.
